prompt: Two exported runs used different feed-line losses. What is needed to isolate the effect of mast height?
options: Average the two receive-level results
Use the result with the higher antenna gain
Apply the same overlay color to both exports
Re-run with common settings except for mast height
explanation: A controlled comparison changes only the input being tested.

prompt: A team has nine individual coverage maps and wants to show the union of usable areas. What should it prepare?
options: A mean of the station-to-station distances
A composite using a common usability rule
A table of tower elevations
An export of the largest single footprint
explanation: The composite combines individual footprints under consistent signal-class criteria.

prompt: A location just beyond the configured plot radius is blank. How should the team interpret it?
options: It has no result in that plot and may require a larger run
It is a measured dead spot
It is necessarily below receiver threshold
It is covered by whichever station is closest
explanation: The plot radius limits the analysis, so an unplotted point needs further evaluation.

prompt: A rerun changes receiver threshold and predicted usable area expands. What changed in the comparison?
options: The antenna height above ground
The actual terrain profile
The cutoff for classifying usable signal
The locations recorded for modeled transmitters
explanation: A changed threshold can reclassify a predicted level without changing the physical path.

prompt: A hypothetical prediction is −92 dBm with a threshold of −103 dBm. What is the predicted margin?
options: 11 dB
10 dB
21 dB
explanation: Subtract the threshold from the receive level. −92 minus −103 gives 11 dB.

prompt: A ridge crosses the direct path, but the link result has positive fade margin. What conclusion fits both readings?
options: The profile must be wrong because the link closes
The positive margin proves unobstructed optical LOS
The ridge has no effect on predicted signal loss
The model predicts a viable obstructed path under those inputs
explanation: The worked study distinguishes link closure from optical clearance and reports links that close by diffraction.

prompt: An optical path has a clear centerline but some nearby terrain intrudes into the Fresnel zone. How should it be recorded?
options: No optical LOS and full Fresnel clearance
An unplotted path with no centerline result
Optical LOS with partial Fresnel clearance
An optical path with guaranteed link closure
explanation: The straight line and the surrounding Fresnel zone have different clearance conditions.

prompt: Two candidate links pass the threshold, but one has substantially less predicted headroom. Which deserves earlier validation if both are equally important?
options: The higher-margin path
The lower-margin path
Whichever result appears first in the deck
The shorter path regardless of margin
explanation: Lower margin offers less headroom if actual conditions differ from the assumptions.

prompt: A team wants to compare cellular operators using model exports. Which approach supports comparison?
options: Treat every mapped tower as though it was modeled
Use a common study extent and document inputs and towers included
Select a different zoom level for each carrier
Assume the best footprint verifies the best actual service
explanation: Documented assumptions, selected sites and a common viewing area make the comparison interpretable.

prompt: A tower pin has no matching coverage layer. What should the map reviewer check first?
options: Whether the tower was included in a model run
Whether the carrier has changed its network name
Whether the image has full opacity
Whether the tower has optical LOS to every other tower
explanation: The exercise distinguishes mapped candidate towers from those with computed predictions.

prompt: A reviewer wants the verified antenna height of an operator's tower. What can the model's antenna height establish?
options: The tower's confirmed installation height
The antenna height of every nearby station
The height assumed by the run
The minimum receiver height for service
explanation: The saved model records an input assumption. Operator records or measurement would be separate evidence.

prompt: An apparent gap appears in a modeled carrier overlay. Which statement is supported without field evidence?
options: The carrier has no active subscribers there
Every phone will fail to connect there
The nearest plotted tower is offline
The modeled runs show no usable service
explanation: A gap is specific to the selected model results and does not establish actual service conditions.

prompt: A candidate relay increases the composite usable area but a small red patch remains. What is the proper description?
options: The relay fully removes the original gap
The model failed because it still shows any gap
Usable coverage improves, but a dead spot remains
The red area confirms hardware failure in the relay
explanation: The before-and-after comparison can show improvement and remaining gaps together.

prompt: A high candidate site reaches several outlying users but misses the required upstream connection. What should the planner conclude?
options: The relay succeeds because it is on high ground
The site alone cannot bridge the two sides
The upstream link can be assumed from the downstream links
Only the downstream coverage area matters
explanation: End-to-end usefulness depends on all required relay legs.

prompt: A map shows two similar relay sites. One appears accessible and the other has uncertain access. What should be done before committing?
options: Choose the uncertain site solely because its contour is slightly larger
Compare only their elevations
Choose whichever appears nearer the center of the map
Verify access along with the link results
explanation: A useful relay needs a workable site and acceptable communications links.

prompt: What comparison isolates the coverage improvement from adding a relay?
options: Compare with and without the relay at one extent and cutoff
Change the signal classes and plot boundary for the second run
Show only the relay footprint in both maps
Use a path-profile screenshot in place of the baseline
explanation: The study's before-and-after comparison uses a shared corridor and classification rule.

prompt: A taller mast offers only a small improvement, and the current setup exceeds the planning margin. What is the reasonable next step?
options: Keep the practical configuration provisionally and verify it in the field
Adopt the tallest mast solely because it scored higher
Treat height as immaterial to all future paths
Replace the model's measured terrain with a flat profile
explanation: Choose configuration based on the benefit to the required link and validate the resulting setup.

prompt: A revised map leaves a residual gap on an assigned route. What should the recommendation include?
options: Treat any coverage improvement as complete resolution
Remove the gap from the map extent
Flag the gap and provide a fallback and field check
Raise the acceptable outage threshold without informing users
explanation: A remaining gap calls for a fallback and verification.

prompt: The cellular model is promising in one area but uncertain outside it. How should the case-study plan treat cellular service?
options: Replace all planned radio links with cellular
Use it as a contingency where suitable, with other means available
Assume availability throughout the operating area
Use tower count alone to choose the communications plan
explanation: The example limits cellular to a contingency because modeled availability is incomplete.

prompt: Field checks show a weaker link than expected. Which record supports a useful model revision?
options: Only a screenshot of the revised legend
The measured ground elevation without the test location
Only a note that the test occurred
Observed signal, field conditions, and modeled path
explanation: Comparing field conditions with model assumptions gives planners a basis for updating the prediction.
